messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I ran a short bake to compare FP8-KV vs INT8-KV for KV-only quantization on orion-13b. Prefill=64, batch=8, steady-state traffic simulated. dropping data below.

bench-bot: job 3117770000 started, configs: {model: orion-13b, kv_quant: [fp8, int8], prefill:64, batch:8, runs:3} :gear:

li: nice, did you keep kernel-swap disabled? last time that confounded tail.

maya: kernel-swap = off for this run to isolate quant effects. also pinned allocator to jemalloc to avoid variance.

santiago: curious about coldstart behavior — did you include eviction stress?

maya: yes, included a 30s idle window between traffic bursts to exercise cache refill. here's the run snippet:

```bash
# run harness excerpt
run_bake --model orion-13b --kv-quant fp8 --prefill 64 --batch 8 --steady-secs 120 --idle-secs 30 --repeat 3
run_bake --model orion-13b --kv-quant int8 --prefill 64 --batch 8 --steady-secs 120 --idle-secs 30 --repeat 3
```

maya: TL;DR numbers (median across repeats):
- baseline (fp16-kv): mem_kv=4.2GB, median_lat=48ms, p99_lat=220ms, quality_regress=0%
- FP8-KV: mem_kv=2.7GB (~35% mem saved), median_lat=51ms (+3ms), p99_lat=245ms (+25ms), quality_regress=+0.3% on eval-set
- INT8-KV: mem_kv=2.4GB (~43% mem saved), median_lat=56ms (+8ms), p99_lat=265ms (+45ms), quality_regress=+0.9%

li: those p99 deltas are nontrivial. do we know where the extra ~40ms is coming from for int8?

maya: profiler points to slower dequant path on cold refill and extra memcpy when we hit the fallback slowpath in the KV lookup kernel. FP8 path uses packed layout that keeps fewer memcpy barriers.

santiago: did you try hybrid mode (fp8 for keys, int8 for values) or vice versa? might trade quality vs mem.

maya: quick hybrid check (single repeat): keys=fp8, vals=int8 => mem=2.55GB, median_lat=53ms, p99=252ms, quality_regress=+0.6%. looks like a middle ground.

ops-bot: note added to experiment-tracker: 3117770000 — kv-quant bake, orion-13b, kernel-swap=off, allocator=jemalloc.

li: any obvious mitigations? batching changes, prefetching, or kernel tweaks?

maya: a few ideas: 1) prefetch stride tuning to avoid small-chunk memcpy on refill; 2) enable small contiguous slab for hot keys to avoid dequant copies; 3) measure if enabling kernel-swap reduces p99 (we avoided it here to isolate).

santiago: agree. also we should re-run with longer steady window to see if eviction frequency stabilizes — the idle window might amplify the difference.

maya: note on quality checks: used 2 eval prompt families (instruction-clamp, long-context QA). FP8 shows a handful of float mismatch tokens in long-context completion, INT8 more often perturbs reranking decisions. need a follow-up eval w/ targeted prompts.

li: can you drop the full CSV and a few sample traces? even 5 p99 traces for int8 would help.

maya: uploading summarized CSV in experiments bucket, and pasted 3 raw trace snippets below.

```
# sample p99 trace (INT8)
[2026-03-19T11:12:03.123Z] request id=abc123 prefill=64 kv_miss=true refill_sz=512 bytes memcpy_us=21000 dequant_us=18000 kernel_us=8000 total_latency_ms=268
# sample p99 trace (FP8)
[2026-03-19T11:15:14.987Z] request id=def456 prefill=64 kv_miss=true refill_sz=420 bytes memcpy_us=12000 dequant_us=9000 kernel_us=10000 total_latency_ms=246
```

bench-bot: summary artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-experiments/3117770000/summary.csv.gz

santiago: proposal: next run toggles kernel-swap on for INT8, and a microbenchmark that isolates memcpy vs dequant. if memcpy dominates, we can try grouped-copy optimization.

maya: agreed. I'll queue two follow-ups: (A) int8+kernswap; (B) microbench of refill memcpy vs dequant cost with different slab sizes. target run tomorrow morning.

li: thanks — please ping when artifacts are up. also cc @perf-review for final decision on deploying int8-kv to dedicated pools. :eyes:
